sentences.text:
1. This Writ Petition is filed questioning the action of the respondents in proposing to construct a hospital in the land of the petitioners admeasuring to an extent of Ac.0.07 guntas, in Sy.No.131,
situated at Haripirala Village, Thorrur Mandal of Mahabubabad District and sought a direction to the respondents not to proceed with any construction activity in the land of the petitioners.

2. Heard the learned Counsel for the petitioners and the learned Assistant Government Pleader for Revenue and the learned Standing Counsel for Gram Panchayats appearing for the respondents and perused the record.
3.

The learned Counsel for the petitioners would submit that one Pulichedu Bujjamma D/o. Mysaiah was assigned land admeasuring to extent of SK, J Ac.0.07 guntas in Sy.No.131 of Haripirala Village of Thorrur Mandal, Mahabubabad District (hereinafter referred to 'subject land') vide Patta No.2128/1994 dated 23.09.1994.
Thereafter the said Bujjamma married to the petitioner No.1 and they were blessed with petitioner Nos.2 to 4.
The petitioners constructed a hut and a shed in the land assigned to them.
The respondents proposed to construct a Government Hospital in the land of the petitioners without following due procedure.

On coming to know of the same, the petitioners approached the respondents and requested them not to permit any construction in the land of the petitioners, but the respondents are determined to construct the hospital in the land of the petitioners.

If the respondents succeed in their efforts to construct the hospital in the land of the petitioners, which was assigned to them thirty years back, the petitioners will be put to hardship and they will remain shelter less and sought a direction to the respondents not to SK, J proceed with the construction of the hospital in the land of the petitioners and requested to allow the writ petition.

4. The learned Assistant Government Pleader for Revenue basing on the counter filed by the respondent No.4 would submit that though Late Pulichedu Bujjamma, wife of the petitioner No.1,
was assigned the subject land through Patta Certificate No.2128/1994 dated 23.09.1994, no Panchanama was prepared by the then Tahsildar with regard to delivery of the subject land.

The total extent of land in Sy.No.131 as per Khasara Pahanai is Ac.30.30 guntas, out of which an extent of Ac.8.32 guntas was already assigned to poor persons and the remaining land to an extent of Ac.21.38 guntas, which is a rocky area.
Out of the balance extent of Ac.21.38 guntas, an extent of Ac.0.07 guntas was allotted for construction of a hospital.

sentences.text: The assignee, who is the wife of the petitioner No.1, died long ago and till date no mutation was granted in favour of the wife of the petitioner No.1 in the revenue record.
Neither the name of the assignee nor the family members of the assignee were recorded in the revenue records.
On 17.10.2020 a Panchanama was conducted and handed over possession of the subject land to the concerned department.

As the subject land has been kept fallow since many years and as Haripirala Village is far from nearby Medical facilities, the respondents have proposed to construct the Health Center in the subject land and there are no merits
and requested to dismiss the writ petition.

5. The learned Standing Counsel for Gram Panchayath, basing on the counter filed by the respondent No.5, would submit that the subject land was assigned to one Late Bujjamma for cultivation and SK, J as a matter of fact the entire land in Sy.No.131, where the Primary Health Sub-Center is being constructed, is a hillock area and not feasible for cultivation.

The Government has already taken a policy for establishment of a minimum health sub-centers for every cluster village and identified the subject land, which is a Government land, for construction of one such Health Center.

The construction of health sub-center has been almost completed except finishing work and in order to stall the construction the petitioners filed the instant writ petition and there are no merits and requested to dismiss the writ petition.

6. After hearing both sides and on perusing the record, this Court is of the considered view that the respondent-authorities have assigned land admeasuring to an extent of Ac.0.07 guntas in Sy.No.131,
situated at Haripirala Village of Thorrur Mandal of Mahabubabad District through Patta SK, J certificate No.2128/1994, dated 23.09.1994 in favour of the wife of the petitioner No.1 and mother of petitioner Nos.2 to 4.

While it being so, the respondent-authorities have taken over possession of the land assigned to the wife of the petitioner No.1 for the purpose construction of Government Hospital (Health sub-centre) without following any process of law, in view of the same the petitioners filed the instant writ petition.

7. The respondent-authorities in their counter are not disputing the assignment of subject land in favour of wife of the petitioner No.1 through Patta certificate No.2128/1994 dated 23.09.1994, but stating that the no panchanama was conducted delivering possession of the subject land and the name of the wife of the 1st petitioner was also not recorded in the Revenue records and in view of the same the subject land was allotted for construction of Health Centre.

Once, the respondent-authorities have admitted in their counter SK, J that patta certificate was granted in favour of the wife of the petitioner No.1 in respect of the subject land and the Revenue authorities have to mutate the records, but the same was not fault on the part of the assignee.

8. The respondents without cancelling the patta certificate granted in favour of wife of the petitioner No.1 and without issuing any resumption proceedings have taken over the possession of the subject land and allotted the same for construction of Health Center stating that out of total extent of Ac.30.03 guntas in Sy.No.131 of Haripirala Village of Thorrur Mandal to an extent of Ac.08.32 guntas was already assigned to poor persons and the remaining land is totally covered with rock area.

Once the respondents admitted in their counter that the land which was allotted to the poor persons, including the wife of the petitioner No.1, is not rocky area, now respondents without Rayapuram Hanmanth vs The State Of Telangana on 5 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166249168/

The patta certificate granted in favour of the wife of the petitioner No.1 is not cancelled by the competent authority and the respondents cannot construct the Health Center in the land assigned to the wife of the petitioner No.1.
9.
As per the counter filed by the respondent No.5, which was filed in the year 2021, stated that the construction of Health Center has been almost completed.

In view of the same, the respondent- authorities have to follow the procedure as contemplated under the Land Acquisition Act and pay compensation to the petitioners for the acquired land or allot alternative land.

10 In view of the above finding, this writ petition is disposed of directing the respondents to initiate Land Acquisition Proceedings in respect of the acquired land SK, J of the petitioners admeasuring to an extent of Ac.0.07 guntas in Sy.No.131, situated at Haripirala Village of Thorrur Mandal, as contemplated under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 and pay compensation to the petitioners or allot alternative land within four (4) months from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
